original_question: Describe all two-orbit polytopes of full rank.
target_in_paper: Section 5.1, Problem 23: "Describe all two-orbit polytopes of full rank." ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the exact target in the paper: it matches the official wording of Problem 23 and keeps the intended scope on two-orbit/full-rank classification, rather than broadening to general k-orbit or nearly full rank questions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))
missing_details: The paper is in the Euclidean realization setting here: the problem concerns polytopes realized in Euclidean space E^d, not an unrestricted abstract classification problem detached from realization theory. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))

Section 5 first defines realizations, faithful realizations, and symmetric realizations, so to make the question stand-alone one should say that the objects under discussion are faithful symmetric Euclidean realizations (geometric polytopes). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))
“Two-orbit” should be unpacked as meaning exactly two flag-orbits; in the paper’s language this is encoded by a symmetry type graph with two vertices. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))

“Full rank” needs the paper’s generalized definition used immediately before Problem 23: an n-polytope in E^d is of full rank if there is no (n+1)-polytope in E^d with the same symmetry type graph. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))

The scope includes both finite and infinite polytopes, as indicated by Problem 22 and the surrounding discussion from which the full-rank notion for Problem 23 is specialized. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))
The quantifiers over the Euclidean dimension d and the rank n are implicit in the draft and should be stated explicitly in a stand-alone formulation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))

No ambient ring/field, polynomial degree, homogeneity, operator, or nilpotency conditions are relevant in this paper’s problem; the missing assumptions are geometric and combinatorial instead. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))
refined_question: Classify, for all Euclidean dimensions d and ranks n, all finite or infinite n-polytopes P admitting faithful symmetric realizations in E^d such that P has exactly two flag-orbits and is of full rank, meaning that if T(P) denotes its symmetry type graph (recording the flag-orbits and their i-adjacencies), then no (n+1)-polytope realized in the same E^d has symmetry type graph T(P). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))
justification: The draft already reproduces the paper’s official Problem 23 almost verbatim, so the needed refinement is not to change the target but to restore the context suppressed by the bare sentence. Section 2.2 supplies the meanings of k-orbit and symmetry type graph, while Section 5 and Section 5.1 place the question inside Euclidean realization theory and give the generalized definition of full rank immediately before Problem 23. I therefore kept the question as narrow as the paper does: Euclidean, realization-theoretic, two-orbit, and full-rank in the symmetry-type-graph sense. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))
